raw_segments.text: 15. In the faith in what? In the love for what? In the hope of what? These weaklings,
they also forsooth wish to be the strong some time, there is no doubt about it, some time
their kingdom also must come. The kingdom of God is their name for it, as has been mentioned.
They are so meek in everything. Yet in order to experience that kingdom it is necessary
to live long, to live beyond death, yes. Eternal life is necessary so that one can
make up forever for that earthly life in faith. In love. In hope.
Make up for what? Make up by what? Dante, as it seems to me, made a crass mistake when with
awe-inspiring ingenuity he placed that inscription over the gate of his hell. Me too made eternal
love. At any rate the following inscription would have a much better right to stand over the gate of
the Christian paradise and its eternal blessedness. Me too made eternal hate, granted of course that
a truth may rightly stand over the gate to a lie. For what is the blessedness of that paradise?
Possibly we could quickly surmise it, but it is better that it should be explicitly
attested by an authority who in such matters is not to be disparaged, Thomas of Aquinas,
the great teacher and saint. Beady in regno celestae, says he, as gently as a lamb,
vied bunt ponas damnatorum, ut beatituto illis magis complaisat. Or if we wish to hear a stronger
tone, a word from the mouth of a triumphant father of the church, who warned his disciples
against the cruel ecstasies of the public spectacles, but why? Faith offers us much more
says he, despectac. C. 29 SS. Something much stronger. Thanks to the redemption,
joys of quite another kind stand at our disposal. Instead of athletes we have our martyrs. We wish
for blood, well, we have the blood of Christ but what then awaits us on the day of his return of
his triumph? And then does he proceed, does this enraptured visionary? At a nim supersunt
aelia spectacular, illa ultimas et perpetus judicae dies, illa nationibus inspiritus,
illa dericis, cum tanta seculi vetustas et tot e Jews nativatates uno in horientor. Qui
tonk spectaculari latituto, quid admirer, quid ridem, you begot him. You by exultum,
spectans tot et tantos reges, qui ensealum recepti nonciobanter, cum ipso jove et ipsis
sways testibus inimis tenibris congemisense. Item presides, the provincial governors, persecutors
deminicide niminis sieveribus, quam ipsi flammis sieverunt insultin tibis contra Cristiano's
liquescence. Quoes praetorias sapiens, illos philosophos quorum, dissipulis sways uniconflagrant
tibis irubescence, quibis nile ad diem pertner suadibent, quibis animas out nullas out non
in prostina corpora redituras affirmabent. Eshium poetas non ad radimantinec ad minwa,
sed ad inapanati Christi tribunal palpitants. Tunk magi's traggio dia diendi, magi's
silicet vocals, with louder tones and more violent shrieks, in sua propria calamitate,
tonk histrion's cognisendi, soluteer's molto per ignum, tonk spectandis origa enflamia rotitotis
rubens, tonk zystisae contemplandi non in gymnassas, sed in ene jackulati, nysae quod
ne tonk quidum illos vellum vivos, ut quimallum ad eus podius conspectum insatiableum confera,
quiendominum severunt. Hygastale, dichem fabri out quistuarii filius, as is shown by the whole
of the following, and in particular by this well-known description of the mother of Jesus
from the Talmud, tertullian is henceforth referring to the Jews. Sabadi destructor,
samarites et demonium habens. Hygast quem ad juda redimistis, hygast ella erindinec calafis
diverberatus, sputimentis de decoratus, fel et acid patatus. Hygast, quem clam descent subrepurant,
ut resorexis dicature vel hortulanus detracts it, ne lacticis sui frequentia commentium
ladder enter, ut talia species, ut talibus exalts, quis tibai praetor out consul out
sacerdos de sua liberallitate prastibit, et tamen heek jam habemus quadimodo per phytum
spiritu imaginante reprisentata, ceterum qualia a la sunt, quinec oculus viditnec oris oddavitnec
in core hamini's ascenderunt. I core roman 2, 9, credo circo et atracavia, first and fourth row
or according to others the comic and the tragic stay, et omni studio gradira, per phytum, so stands it written.
